# How This Book Is Written {.unnumbered}

A book about AI-assisted engineering should be candid about how it was made.
I began the project during an academic sabbatical to pursue a question I had
been circling for several years. I chose to develop it in public because I do
not want to write about how AI changes engineering only from a distance.
Working with these systems every day has made both their value and their
failure modes harder to romanticize. The public draft lets me test the
synthesis against current research and reader feedback, and it keeps me
returning to the evidence as new work appears.

The process described in this book has also shaped how I write it. I formulate
a question, explore alternatives, implement a draft, evaluate it against the
sources and what a reader needs from the chapter, interpret what failed, and
decide what to retain or revise. The analogy only goes so far. Writing a
synthesis lecture is not the same as designing a chip, and the writing process
does not produce physical measurements or validate the book's technical
claims. Still, the same discipline helps. I record what changed, how I checked
it, and why I kept or rejected it.

I use generative systems because I want firsthand experience of where they
help and where they fail. They help me consider alternative structures, find
adjacent work for closer reading, challenge an assumption, and try another
explanation when the first one fails. Their greatest contribution is breadth.
They can place ideas from computer architecture, machine learning, electronic
design automation, software engineering, and experimental practice beside one
another quickly. That is useful, but it is not yet synthesis. The harder work
is deciding what transfers across fields, what breaks under architecture
constraints, and what coherent perspective remains.

I learned the danger most clearly when I allowed output to outrun review. The
prose became smoother while the argument became weaker. Sections accumulated
repeated ideas, attractive terms without stable meanings, and citations that
did not always support the precise claim being made. Repairing those failures
meant returning to the purpose of the chapter, reading the sources again, and
sometimes discarding substantial changes. More generation did not remove the
need for judgment. It increased the amount of material that required it.

That experience also clarified my role. I decide which distinctions matter,
what the evidence supports, where an analogy fails, what belongs in the
argument, and what should be left out. My role begins before anything is
generated. I frame the questions, select and interpret the evidence, connect
the ideas, and decide what the book says. Responsibility for the result remains
mine.

Writing is also how I test whether I understand a subject well enough to teach
it. When an explanation cannot survive a reader's questions, the synthesis is
not finished. This remains a working manuscript, and I expect it to change as
the argument and evidence improve. If you find a passage that is vague,
imprecise, or wrong, or a connection that deserves a harder test, please
[reach out](https://vijay.seas.harvard.edu).

Vijay Janapa Reddi
